headline: Putin meets Chinese Premier Li Qiang in St. Petersburg
dek: Putin met Chinese Premier Li Qiang at Constantine Palace, St. Petersburg (Oct 21) — the same palace where he met US envoy Witkoff earlier that day.
sources: Xinhua/TASS (via Al Mayadeen English); Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov
fault_line: A three-way summit that could finally end the war — or a great-power carve-up of Ukraine without Zelensky at the table?

sections.what_happened: Putin met Chinese Premier Li Qiang at Constantine Palace, St. Petersburg (Oct 21) — the same palace where he met US envoy Witkoff earlier that day. The two sides signed a package of cooperation documents covering trade, aerospace, science, technology, education; agreed to expand AI, biotech, digital economy cooperation and Arctic shipping freight. Bilateral trade exceeded $185B in the first 8 months of 2026 (+28.4% y/y, per Chinese embassy in Russia); national-currency settlement approaching 100%; Power of Siberia operating stably; Deputy PM Novak said Power of Baikal (Power of Siberia 2) agreements could be finalized by year-end once companies complete commercial negotiations. Li: China-Russia coordination is a 'precious stabilizing force'; Beijing ready to deepen coordination within SCO and BRICS. Kremlin aide Ushakov: a possible first-ever meeting of the leaders of China, Russia and the United States is being prepared, aiming to include it in next month's Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen, China.
sections.what_verified: Xinhua and TASS agree on the meeting, the package of documents, trade figures and the Shenzhen trilateral summit preparation. Li delegation list published (Wu Zhenglong, Zheng Shanjie, Wang Wentao, Ma Zhaoxu et al.).
sections.what_disputed: Ushakov's trilateral-summit claim is single-sourced to the Kremlin via Chinese state media; no US confirmation located. 'Being prepared' is proposal-stage language, not an agreed summit.
sections.why_matters: The $185B number is the real story: while Washington holds sanctions during 'delicate negotiations', Moscow and Beijing are wiring the world's second-biggest trade corridor into national currencies — sanctions-proof by design. If a Shenzhen three-way happens, Ukraine's terms get negotiated over a table it doesn't sit at.
sections.context: Background: NEW — Putin meets Chinese Premier Li Qiang in St. Petersburg; possible first-ever China-Russia-US leaders summit being prepared for Shenzhen APEC

totw_analysis: Our read: The $185B number is the real story: while Washington holds sanctions during 'delicate negotiations', Moscow and Beijing are wiring the world's second-biggest trade corridor into national currencies — sanctions-proof by design. If a Shenzhen three-way happens, Ukraine's terms get negotiated over a table it doesn't sit at. The fault line our audience is arguing over: A three-way summit that could finally end the war — or a great-power carve-up of Ukraine without Zelensky at the table?
